title: Privacy, Robustness, and Fairness Trade-offs in Federated Intrusion Detection: Geometric Indistinguishability at the Aggregation Interface

C-a.quote: clients implement Differentially Private SGD (DP-SGD) [1], which modifies standard SGD through two operations: (i) per-sample gradient clipping to bound L2sensitivity by C; and (ii) calibrated Gaussian noise injection ... For robustness, the server applies coordinate-wise median aggregation [21], which computes the element-wise median across client updates.
C-a.locator: Sections 3.2 and 3.3 (Mechanisms). EXACTLY ONE COMPONENT CARRIES A DEFENSE PURPOSE: the coordinate-wise median, introduced with that purpose in the second span ("For robustness, the server applies..."). THE DP-SGD STAGE AND ITS CLIPPING ARE PRIVACY-PURPOSED AND AMENDMENT 3 EXCISES BOTH: the first span states the purpose as achieving (eps, delta)-privacy and names clipping's job as bounding L2 sensitivity, and the introduction says the same thing again, "is widely adopted to bound this leakage, providing (ε, δ)-privacy guarantees by clipping per-sample gradients and injecting calibrated Gaussian noise [6,8], albeit at utility cost.". No sentence anywhere in the paper gives clipping, the Gaussian noise, the pos_weight loss reweighting or the ten-client IID partitioning a purpose of resisting faulty, malicious or poisoned updates. The paper itself treats the two mechanisms as belonging to different literatures, "These mechanisms are often evaluated separately in federated learning.", and its own robustness sentence assigns the whole defensive job to the aggregation rule, "Byzantine-robust aggregation rules, such as coordinate-wise median [17] or Krum [5], address this by filtering statistical outliers, contracting the acceptance region around honest consensus". The composition is real and is applied to the same round -- DP-SGD on the client, median on the server -- but only one member of it is counted, so C-a's "two or more" is not met. THIS IS THE SAME EXCISION REASON AS Byz-Clip21-SGD2M (2603.23472), NOT A NEW ONE.

C-b.quote: Aggregation is fixed to Coordinatewise Median, which was selected for its stability and minimal degradation under 40% pressure (0.3% F1 drop) compared to alternatives like Krum or Trimmed Mean in pre-validation (Figure 4). This selection isolates privacy-fairness interactions from aggregation-induced variance.
C-b.locator: Section 4.3. This is the closest thing in the paper to a constituent-property reason and it does not qualify, for the reason settled on Byz-Clip21-SGD2M and PRoVeFL: the reason selects ONE counted defense to sit beside an EXCISED privacy mechanism, so it is not a reason for pairing two counted constituents, and with one counted constituent there is no qualifying pairing to motivate. Recorded because the sentence is nonetheless the frame's most literal statement of selection by STANDALONE EFFECTIVENESS -- the rule is chosen on its own pre-composition degradation under 40% adversarial pressure, measured across four rules in Figure 4, "Fig. 4. F1 Score Across Aggregation Rules (FedAvg, Krum, Median, Trimmed Mean) Under Clean, 20%, and 40% Adversarial Client Ratios.", and then held fixed for every reported experiment. The companion separability move is at Section 4.1, "To isolate the geometric interaction between privacy and robustness from data heterogeneity, we partition the dataset across ten clients using IID sam". No quotation gives a complementary-threat-coverage reason: the three properties the paper composes are privacy, robustness and class-wise fairness, which are PROPERTIES of the system rather than two defense constituents.

C-c.quote: We evaluate two attack vectors: (1) Label-flip poisoning (untargeted data poisoning where labels are inverted); and (2) Gaussian model poisoning (direct corruption of update vectors via N (0, 5.02) noise). ... DIclass decreases from 0.750 in the non-private setting to 0.516 in the clean private setting, and falls further under attack (e.g., 0.581 under 40% label flipping and 0.509 under model poisoning).
C-c.locator: Sections 4.3 and 5.2; the metrics are the composed system's own F1, per-class detection rate and class-wise disparate impact, reported under label-flip and Gaussian model poisoning at 0%, 20% and 40% malicious clients and at four privacy budgets. THE STRING "ASR" OCCURS 0 TIMES IN 39379 CHARACTERS AND SO DO "attack success" AND "robust accuracy", BUT THE REFERENT IS PRESENT: performance under attack of the assembled DP-SGD + median system is what every result figure reports, which is what C-c asks for. The headline ladder is at Section 5.2, "performance degrades more gradually as privacy becomes stronger: F1 declines from 0.9537 at ϵ = ∞ to 0.7379 at ϵ = 1.0, while DIclass decreases from 0.750 to 0.205.", and the per-class floor at Section 5.3 and Figure 8, "factual collapse, it does not remove the empirical signal-to-noise boundary induced by strong DP noise for extremely rare events.".

C-d.quote: performance degrades more gradually as privacy becomes stronger: F1 declines from 0.9537 at ϵ = ∞ to 0.7379 at ϵ = 1.0, while DIclass decreases from 0.750 to 0.205.
C-d.locator: Section 5.2 and Figure 5. The upstream stage is varied as a GRADED DOSE -- eps in {infinity, 5.0, 3.0, 1.0} -- while the downstream mechanism is held fixed by explicit design decision, "This selection isolates privacy-fairness interactions from aggregation-induced variance.", and the attacks are held fixed; an adversarial outcome is read at each setting, "DIclass decreases from 0.750 in the non-private setting to 0.516 in the clean private setting, and falls further under attack (e.g., 0.581 under 40% label flipping and 0.509 under model poisoning).". THE MANIPULATION IS CONFOUNDED BY DESIGN AND THE PAPER SAYS SO: the client learning rate is a declared function of eps (Figure 1's schedule and Figure 3), justified at Section 4.2, "DP-SGD noise requires smaller learning rates to maintain convergence stability [1]. Theoretically, the optimal learning rate η scales inversely with the noise multiplier σ to preserve the gradient signal-to-noise ratio [2]. Our schedule (Fig 3) instantiates this principle for the FL-NIDS setting.". So two things move together along the ladder, and the paper demonstrates that this matters -- under a static LR = 0.05 the same ladder produces collapse rather than a graded decline, Section 5.1, "we identify catastrophic fairness collapse at ϵ = 1.0 under a static learning rate of LR = 0.05". Rule 4 (C-d gets benefit of the doubt) carries the code: the experiment plausibly holds a downstream mechanism fixed while varying an upstream stage, and it does, imperfectly. The COMPONENT-CONTRAST route is absent by the authors' choice, not by omission -- Figure 4's four aggregation rules vary the DOWNSTREAM rule at a single condition as pre-validation, and the eps x aggregation-rule cross is never run; the paper's own limitations section names the gap, "Second, the restriction to coordinate-wise median aggregation limits immediate generalization to other Byzantine-robust rules like Krum or FLTrust.".

C-e.quote: strong DP noise (σ = 0.189) suppresses minority gradients irrespective of architecture, establishing a privacy-induced floor. ... as DP-SGD increases the dispersion of honest minority updates, robust aggregation may attenuate those updates more strongly when they become statistically atypical relative to the dominant client update pattern.
C-e.locator: Sections 6.2 and 6.3; the first span attributes an outcome to a named constituent (the DP noise, at a quoted noise multiplier) and the second states the mechanism by which the two constituents jointly produce it. The paper hedges the claim in three places rather than asserting a law, and the hedges are part of the evidence: "we use this idea as an interpretive hypothesis rather than a formal theorem or directly estimated decision rule." (Section 3.4), "We therefore interpret the results as evidence of a threshold-like degradation regime under joint privacy and robustness constraints, rather than as a formally established phase transition." (Section 5.2) and "This is a configuration-specific empirical observation rather than a proof of a universal privacy limit." (Section 5.3).

coder_note:
PRIMARY = NO AND DESIGN = NO, ON C-a ALONE, AND THE ROW IS STILL THE MOST USEFUL EXTERNAL EXHIBIT IN THE FRAME FOR A3. Under Amendment 3 the composition has one counted member: DP-SGD's clipping and Gaussian noise are privacy-purposed on the paper's own words, so the coordinate-wise median stands alone and C-a fails. That is the same excision reason as Byz-Clip21-SGD2M (2603.23472) and adds no new kind. What makes the row valuable is everything downstream of that code.

THE PAPER STATES OUR PREMISE IN ITS ABSTRACT AND ITS CONCLUSION. "Existing literature treats these properties as independently composable, an assumption that this paper challenges both theoretically and empirically." (Abstract) and "privacy, robustness, and class-wise threat coverage should be evaluated jointly in federated NIDS rather than treated as independently composable properties." (Section 8). This is the frame's most explicit external statement that composability is an assumption rather than a fact, and unlike DP-BR-FedAvg (2609.03064) it is put as the paper's whole subject rather than as one finding. A3 must quote it and then say precisely what we add, because the axes differ: they compose PRIVACY with a defense and measure a class-coverage cost; we compose a DEFENSE with a DEFENSE and measure whether the ORDERING of defense arms survives composition. Their outcome variable is a gap (majority versus minority coverage); ours is a ranking.

AND IT DECLINES THE IDENTIFYING CROSS IN ONE SENTENCE, WITH A REASON. "Aggregation is fixed to Coordinatewise Median, which was selected for its stability and minimal degradation under 40% pressure (0.3% F1 drop) compared to alternatives like Krum or Trimmed Mean in pre-validation (Figure 4). This selection isolates privacy-fairness interactions from aggregation-induced variance." Figure 4 is a four-rule comparison -- "Fig. 4. F1 Score Across Aggregation Rules (FedAvg, Krum, Median, Trimmed Mean) Under Clean, 20%, and 40% Adversarial Client Ratios." -- run once, at one condition, as PRE-VALIDATION, and used to pick the rule that is then frozen for every reported result. So the paper has both factors on the bench: a four-rule downstream axis and a four-rung upstream privacy ladder. It never crosses them, and the stated reason for not crossing them is that crossing them would introduce "aggregation-induced variance" into the privacy-fairness estimate. That is the separability assumption Prop. prop:identification_full is about, written down as a methods decision by authors whose abstract challenges separability on a different axis. THIS IS NOT A CONTRADICTION AND A3 MUST NOT PRESENT IT AS ONE: they challenge composability where they measured it and assume it where they did not. Stated that way it is the cleanest available demonstration that the assumption is load-bearing in ordinary practice.

THE PAPER ALSO NAMES THE MISSING CELL ITSELF, WHICH MAKES THE EXHIBIT SELF-EVIDENCING. "Second, the restriction to coordinate-wise median aggregation limits immediate generalization to other Byzantine-robust rules like Krum or FLTrust." (Section 7) and, in the same section, "development must shift toward fairness-constrained aggregation designs capable of distinguishing privacy-perturbed minority gradients from adversarial outliers.". Ranking of the three cheapest counterfactuals for A4, in order: PRoVeFL's missing cell (2607.06612) first, then THIS row -- because both factors are already implemented and the cross is one loop -- then STAR-FL's three uncrossed tables (2608.14861).

AN ORDERING REVERSAL IS TABULATED, BUT OVER ARCHITECTURES, NOT DEFENSES. Table 2 crosses eps in {1.0, 3.0, infinity} with five attack scenarios and reports which of two models wins each cell, and the winner changes with the upstream privacy dose: at eps = 1.0 both collapse in the clean and model-poisoning cells while "CMS achieves a 3.3× fairness gain over MLP (0.67 vs 0.41)" under 40% label flipping; "At moderate privacy (ϵ = 3.0), CMS wins all comparisons (5/5), with a maximum +0.044 advantage"; and at the other end "CMS maintains a small edge in clean settings (∆ = +0.017), but MLP outperforms under adversarial conditions (3/4 wins), where architectural simplicity aids recovery.". So the RANKING OF TWO CANDIDATE COMPONENTS INVERTS AS A FUNCTION OF AN UPSTREAM STAGE'S DOSE -- the same shape as our sign reversal, over a different pair of objects. What it does not licence, stated so A3 cannot overreach: the objects are two ARCHITECTURES (a Cortical Memory System and an MLP), not two defense rules; there are no seeds, no intervals and no repeated runs; the reported deltas at eps = 1.0 clean and under model poisoning are -0.0004 and -0.0005, which the paper itself calls a Tie; and the paper says the CMS arm is "a preliminary, fixed configuration rather than the output of an exhaustive hyperparameter search" in its own limitations. Under app:sixcell's standard this is not a demonstrated reversal. It is a precedent for the QUESTION, and the answer to "has anyone measured whether the ordering survives?" remains no for defense pairs.

A NEW HAZARD FOR OUR OWN DOSE LADDERS, AND THE FIRST DELIBERATELY CONFOUNDED C-d IN THE FRAME. The eps ladder co-varies with the client learning rate by design, and the paper shows the ladder's qualitative shape depends on that co-varying parameter: static LR gives "catastrophic fairness collapse", the eps-dependent schedule gives a graded decline. Same upstream doses, two different dose-response readings. Our ladders hold everything but kappa fixed, so this is not a defect we share -- but it is an independent reason a measured dose response is not self-interpreting, and it is worth one clause in A3 next to the composition-invariance argument. A5 must record it as the first C-d in the frame whose manipulation is confounded on the paper's own account, coded YES under rule 4 with the confound disclosed.

(i) The Figure 1 caption is split mid-word by the adjacent column: pdftotext yields "gation Interface: DP-SGD Noise and Byzantine Fil" and then "tering Jointly Suppress Minority-Class Updates.", so the caption's claim (DP-SGD noise and Byzantine filtering jointly suppress minority-class updates) cannot be quoted as one span at all. (ii) Table 1's related-work matrix shatters the sentence that would have been the natural C-b candidate -- the checkmark grid, the row labels and the legend all interleave into "these works treat privacy, ... robustness, and fairness as independently composable proper ... ties rather than interacting con ... straints" -- which is why the C-b and A3 quotations are taken from the Abstract instead, where the same claim is contiguous. (iii) Figure 8's caption interleaves with the Section 6.5 prose, which is why the calibration-floor span has to begin mid-word at "factual collapse". VENUE AND PROVENANCE: accepted at the 8th International Conference on Machine Learning for Cyber Security 2026, with that line as a running header on every page; UNSW-NB15 (175,341 samples), 10 IID clients, 20 rounds, minimum 8 participants. Contribution framing, for the record: "Using UNSW-NB15 with DP-SGD and coordinate-wise median under labelflip and model-poisoning attacks, we provide initial empirical evidence that joint privacy and robustness constraints can disproportionately degrade rareattack coverage, and that some apparent collapse may be attributable to hyperparameter miscalibration rather than an inherent impossibility."
